# Kujo Docs

A local-first path through the Kujo language and ecosystem.

- [Kujo Docs](https://docs.kujolang.ai/) — The shortest path from language basics to reviewable, local-first software.
- [Build](https://docs.kujolang.ai/build/) — Kujo build documentation.
- [Manage Agent Credentials and Connectors](https://docs.kujolang.ai/build/agent-credentials/) — Store reusable provider keys safely, configure project overrides, and connect Kujo Agent Projects without putting secrets in commands or Git.
- [Operate and Harden Agent Projects](https://docs.kujolang.ai/build/agent-operations/) — Diagnose, inspect, run, evaluate, automate, and isolate a repository-owned Kujo Agent Project.
- [Choose an Agent Project Profile](https://docs.kujolang.ai/build/agent-profiles/) — Select the smallest Kujo Agent Project profile that matches the tools, knowledge, workflow, isolation, and observability you need.
- [AI and agents](https://docs.kujolang.ai/build/ai-and-agents/) — Move from a repository-owned agent or normalized model call to tools, approvals, handoffs, and local state.
- [Applications and publishing](https://docs.kujolang.ai/build/applications-and-publishing/) — Choose a copyable application surface for chat, APIs, content, or deterministic static publishing.
- [Editorial publishing](https://docs.kujolang.ai/build/editorial-publishing/) — Move a commissioned idea through evidence, review, packaging, approval, publication, and learning.
- [Knowledge and retrieval](https://docs.kujolang.ai/build/knowledge-and-retrieval/) — Ingest local knowledge and answer with namespaces, citations, and offline fallbacks.
- [Repository-owned Agent Projects](https://docs.kujolang.ai/build/owned-agent-projects/) — Install Kujo's agent platform, create a repository-owned agent, and prove its local lifecycle.
- [Publishing House operator](https://docs.kujolang.ai/build/publishing-house-operator/) — Run publication-profile-driven editorial work through a resumable, policy-bound Kujo control loop.
- [Web operations](https://docs.kujolang.ai/build/web-operations/) — Move from site source to crawl evidence, search data, content relationships, browser proof, and bounded fixes.
- [Workflows and approvals](https://docs.kujolang.ai/build/workflows-and-approvals/) — Turn a sequence of steps into bounded, resumable, and auditable work.
- [Choose a path](https://docs.kujolang.ai/choose-a-path/) — Start with an intent and one small next step instead of browsing the whole ecosystem.
- [Collections](https://docs.kujolang.ai/collections/) — Kujo collections documentation.
- [Agents](https://docs.kujolang.ai/collections/agents/) — Reusable role contracts, chain of command, and evidence expectations.
- [Benchmarks](https://docs.kujolang.ai/collections/benchmarks/) — Benchmark methodology, fixtures, scorecards, and reproducibility limits.
- [Skills](https://docs.kujolang.ai/collections/skills/) — Install, select, and validate Kujo-specific Agent Skills.
- [Workflows](https://docs.kujolang.ai/collections/workflows/) — Browse runnable workflow packs and the artifact each workflow leaves behind.
- [Ecosystem](https://docs.kujolang.ai/ecosystem/) — Kujo ecosystem documentation.
- [Core / Foundation](https://docs.kujolang.ai/ecosystem/core-foundation/) — The Kujo runtime, package, execution, and collaboration foundation.
- [Primitives](https://docs.kujolang.ai/ecosystem/primitives/) — Reusable contracts for agents, evaluation, retrieval, orchestration, privacy, decisions, boundaries, and supervision.
- [Providers](https://docs.kujolang.ai/ecosystem/providers/) — Choose and install a Kujo provider package, then move from a first request to native features.
- [Showcases](https://docs.kujolang.ai/ecosystem/showcases/) — Proof applications demonstrating complete local workflows and product surfaces.
- [Tooling](https://docs.kujolang.ai/ecosystem/tooling/) — Supporting tools for execution, evidence, web operations, editorial production, review, and release gates.
- [Install Kujo](https://docs.kujolang.ai/install/) — Install Kujo v1.1.0 and the tool group you need, or build the CLI from source.
- [Learn](https://docs.kujolang.ai/learn/) — Kujo learn documentation.
- [AI runtime basics](https://docs.kujolang.ai/learn/ai-runtime/) — See the shared controls for provider calls, replay, budgets, secrets, and egress.
- [Capabilities and safe execution](https://docs.kujolang.ai/learn/capabilities/) — Grant only the filesystem, clock, network, or process access a local task actually needs.
- [Editor and CLI support](https://docs.kujolang.ai/learn/editor-support/) — Use the CLI, LSP, and editor adapters to keep feedback close to the file you are editing.
- [Language basics](https://docs.kujolang.ai/learn/language-basics/) — Learn the small set of Kujo syntax and program shapes needed to read a real file.
- [Packages with Kennel](https://docs.kujolang.ai/learn/packages/) — Keep manifests, lockfiles, source policy, and trust decisions deterministic.
- [How the runtime works](https://docs.kujolang.ai/learn/runtime/) — Understand the VM-first execution path, interpreter fallback, and the role of the CLI.
- [Quickstart](https://docs.kujolang.ai/quickstart/) — Create one Kujo file, run it with the VM-first runtime, and check the source.
- [Reference](https://docs.kujolang.ai/reference/) — Find CLI, language, standard-library, configuration, and generated source reference surfaces.
- [Release boundaries](https://docs.kujolang.ai/release-boundaries/) — Read the difference between release-ready within scope, preview, dogfood, and technical showcase.
- [Review](https://docs.kujolang.ai/review/) — Kujo review documentation.
- [Browser, architecture, and privacy checks](https://docs.kujolang.ai/review/browser-architecture-and-privacy/) — Keep browser evidence, dependency boundaries, and redaction in the same release conversation.
- [Context and task contracts](https://docs.kujolang.ai/review/context-and-task-contracts/) — Turn an open-ended request into a structured contract with scope, acceptance, and evidence.
- [Evidence and run history](https://docs.kujolang.ai/review/evidence-and-run-history/) — Preserve the receipt, failure bundle, usage, and handoff that explain what happened.
- [Quality and release gates](https://docs.kujolang.ai/review/quality-and-release-gates/) — Check drift, boundaries, release readiness, browser behavior, and sensitive values before shipping.
- [Tests and evaluation](https://docs.kujolang.ai/review/tests-and-evaluation/) — Run deterministic acceptance checks locally or in CI and keep the expected result explicit.
- [Security model](https://docs.kujolang.ai/security/) — Understand capability gates, local boundaries, secrets, network access, and safe execution wording.
- [Showcases](https://docs.kujolang.ai/showcases/) — Kujo showcases documentation.
- [AI Chat](https://docs.kujolang.ai/showcases/ai-chat/) — A local multi-provider chat application with encrypted profiles, streaming, transcription, and fixture mode.
- [Cinch](https://docs.kujolang.ai/showcases/cinch/) — A local development harness for files, Git, commands, AI context, tools, and proof.
- [CMS](https://docs.kujolang.ai/showcases/cms/) — A framework-neutral content backend with first-class administration, extensions, SEO, identity, AI abilities, MCP, and WebMCP.
- [CRUD API Showcase](https://docs.kujolang.ai/showcases/crud-api/) — A SQLite API and frontend playground showing auth strategies, recovery patterns, and contracts.
- [Intake](https://docs.kujolang.ai/showcases/intake/) — Normalize inbound work, route it through policy, and require approval before external effects.
- [SSG](https://docs.kujolang.ai/showcases/ssg/) — Deterministic Markdown-to-site publishing with templates, feeds, sitemap, and llms.txt.
- [TotalRecall](https://docs.kujolang.ai/showcases/totalrecall/) — A local-first ingestion showcase for meetings, chat exports, Slack threads, and GitHub activity.
- [Start here](https://docs.kujolang.ai/start-here/) — Choose the shortest path from discovering Kujo to running a program or repository-owned agent.
- [Support](https://docs.kujolang.ai/support/) — Find the right place to ask for help, report a problem, or verify a local failure.
- [Tools](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/) — Kujo tools documentation.
- [Agents SDK](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/agents-sdk/) — Build agents with tools, approvals, handoffs, tracing, stores, and budgets.
- [AI SDK](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/ai-sdk/) — Use normalized chat and embedding contracts with fixtures, retries, and redaction.
- [AssetWorks](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/assetworks/) — Plan media assets and preserve provenance, accessibility records, and checksums.
- [BluePencil](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/bluepencil/) — Record structured editorial reviews, verdicts, disagreements, and calibration evidence.
- [CaseFile](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/casefile/) — Capture a failure as a reproducible evidence bundle.
- [ChangeBucket](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/changebucket/) — Measure change footprint, categories, and blast radius.
- [Commerce](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/commerce/) — Add provider-agnostic catalog and checkout contracts to Kujo static sites.
- [Concord](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/concord/) — Find drift across code, docs, examples, specs, and generated artifacts.
- [ContentGraph](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/contentgraph/) — Build an inspectable graph of content relationships, clusters, gaps, and link opportunities.
- [Dispatch](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/dispatch/) — Orchestrate resumable, approved, and auditable workflows.
- [Dossier](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/dossier/) — Preserve claims, sources, evidence, quotations, consent, rights, and freshness.
- [Eval](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/eval/) — Run deterministic acceptance checks locally or in CI.
- [Fence](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/fence/) — Check architecture boundaries and import rules.
- [GalleyPack](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/galleypack/) — Bind editorial artifacts into versioned, checksum-backed production packages.
- [Howl](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/howl/) — Render verified examples into Markdown, HTML, SVG, gallery, and caption assets.
- [Kennel](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/kennel/) — Manage deterministic manifests, dependencies, lockfiles, and trust policy.
- [Kujo](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/kujo/) — Write and run local-first Kujo programs.
- [Leash](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/leash/) — Supervise local AI agents through policy-gated approvals and a mobile control plane.
- [Lens](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/lens/) — Review browser behavior with screenshots, accessibility, links, and flows.
- [MCP](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/mcp/) — Generate guarded MCP servers with roots, limits, auth, and safety tiers.
- [Muzzle](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/muzzle/) — Run noisy workflows quietly while preserving complete logs and summaries.
- [PackWrite](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/packwrite/) — Compile repeatable agent execution packs from context and prompts.
- [PatchBrief](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/patchbrief/) — Turn a diff into a reviewable summary and handoff.
- [PressWire](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/presswire/) — Execute approval-gated publication effects with idempotency and receipts.
- [RAG](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/rag/) — Build local retrieval flows with namespaces, citations, and offline fallbacks.
- [ReaderSignal](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/readersignal/) — Record privacy-bounded audience measurements, feedback, comparisons, and learning.
- [Redact](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/redact/) — Produce deterministic, review-required redactions for local text and Markdown.
- [Relay](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/relay/) — Compose and run bounded agent missions with lifecycle control and verifiable evidence.
- [RunLedger](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/runledger/) — Record run metadata, usage, cost, verdicts, and follow-ups.
- [Scent](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/scent/) — Package focused, bounded, and redacted context for a task.
- [Scout](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/scout/) — Build a structured map of an unfamiliar repository.
- [SearchBridge](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/searchbridge/) — Normalize search, analytics, performance, keyword, backlink, and submission providers.
- [ShipCheck](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/shipcheck/) — Scan release readiness and produce a gate report.
- [SiteKit](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/site-kit/) — Vendor an accessible, semantic, token-driven design system for static sites.
- [SiteProbe](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/siteprobe/) — Crawl a bounded website surface and preserve deterministic intelligence evidence.
- [Source](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/source/) — Coordinate agent-first software work, evidence, decisions, and canonical Git state.
- [Spec](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/spec/) — Turn a request into a structured, checkable task contract.
- [StoryDesk](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/storydesk/) — Plan editorial work with immutable ideas, commissions, assignments, handoffs, and queues.
- [Tribunal](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/tribunal/) — Turn consequential proposals into adversarial, replayable decision evidence.
- [VersionSeal](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/versionseal/) — Bind human approval and authority to an exact checksum-verified version.
- [Ward](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/ward/) — Monitor Dependabot alerts locally and prepare reviewable remediation plans.
- [Watchdog](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/watchdog/) — Observe AI requests, tools, costs, latency, errors, and audit events.
- [Workcell](https://docs.kujolang.ai/tools/workcell/) — Run bounded Kujo and agent workflows in disposable Docker or Podman worktrees.
